e.etymology: A modern American name that joins Bren-, as in Brenna and Brenda, to the -lee ending; a sister form of Brinley and Brynlee.
A modern elaboration that reads as Sarah with the -aya ending of Amaya and Samaya; Saraya is the plainer spelling.
A respelling of Wiley or Wylie, surnames that come from English place names and, in Scotland, from a pet form of William.
From Arabic kanz, treasure. Kinza is used as a girl's name mainly in Pakistan, and Kenza is the North African form.
A spelling of Kamari, a modern American name in the family of Amari, Jamari and Kamaria.

e.meaning: shrewd, knowing; also short for Savannah
e.etymology: A pet form of Savannah and the English word for practical know-how, which came through pidgin English from Spanish or Portuguese sabe, he knows.
Made known by Australian conservationist Bindi Irwin; her father Steve Irwin said it is an Aboriginal word for young girl. In Hindi a bindi is the dot worn on the forehead, from Sanskrit bindu, drop.
namesakes: Bindi Irwin (Australian wildlife conservationist and TV host)

assoc.t: Bindi Irwin, daughter of Crocodile Hunter Steve Irwin
bindi, the forehead dot worn in South Asia

e.etymology: From the Quranic phrase hur in, the fair, wide-eyed companions promised in paradise. The name is especially popular in Pakistan.
A recent American coinage that adds the Ja- prefix to Kyrie, the name made popular by NBA guard Kyrie Irving.
In Tagalog and Kapampangan mythology Mayari is the goddess of the moon, a daughter of the supreme god Bathala. Mayari is also a town in eastern Cuba.
The English adjective, from Latin solaris, of the sun, from sol. It joins Sol, Soleil and Nova among sky words used as names.
A recent American name that blends the sounds of Kamari and Amiri.

e.meaning: from the name of Thor, the Norse thunder god
e.etymology: A Scandinavian name, the Latinized form of Old Danish Thyrvi, built on the name of the god Thor. In the US it also arose separately as a modern coinage beside Tyrone and Tyrell.
namesakes: Tyra Banks (supermodel and host of America's Next Top Model)

assoc.t: Tyra Banks, supermodel and TV host

e.etymology: A z spelling of Lisette, the French pet form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. In the US it is most common in Hispanic families.
A spelling of Danny, the pet form of Daniel and Danielle, from Hebrew Daniyel, God is my judge. The -ie spelling was the usual one for both sexes in the early 1900s.
From Greek Korinna, probably from kore, maiden. It was the name of an ancient Greek lyric poet, and Ovid used it for the woman he addresses in his Amores.
A Slavic name of Bulgar origin, first borne by Boris I, the 9th-century ruler who made Bulgaria Christian. Its root is debated; Turkic words for wolf or snow leopard are the usual candidates.
namesakes: Boris Karloff (actor who played Frankenstein's monster)
e.note: In American pop culture Boris is a stock name for a Russian villain, as in Boris Badenov of Rocky and Bullwinkle.

assoc.t: Boris Johnson, former British prime minister
Boris, the bumbling spy of Rocky and Bullwinkle

e.etymology: A spelling of Kaylee or Kayleigh, a modern name built from Kay and the -lee ending. Kayleigh spread in the 1980s after a hit song by the British band Marillion.

e.meaning: son of Pritha, a name of Arjuna
e.etymology: From Sanskrit Partha, son of Pritha, an epithet of the hero Arjuna in the Mahabharata. Krishna addresses him by it throughout the Bhagavad Gita.

e.meaning: miracle, marvel (Hindi); also a spelling of charisma
e.etymology: In India, a form of Karishma, miracle or marvel, from Persian and probably from Greek kharisma, gift of grace. In the US it is also a K spelling of the English word charisma.
Used as a short form of Viviana and as a sister to Vianna and Vianney. Viana is also a Portuguese and Spanish place name and surname.
From Arabic muhsin, beneficent or charitable, from ahsana, to do well or act rightly. It shares a root with Hassan and Ihsan.
A respelling of Eloise, the English form of French Heloise, from an old Germanic name usually analyzed as hale, healthy, plus wide. The double l points to the nickname Ellie.
A phonetic respelling of Elena, the Spanish, Italian and Slavic form of Helen, from Greek Helene, often explained as torch or bright one.

e.meaning: from a pet form of Hugh: mind, spirit
e.etymology: From Huchon, a medieval pet form of Hugh, a Germanic name meaning mind or spirit. It lives on in the surnames Hutchins and Hutchinson, for which Hutch is the usual nickname.

assoc.t: Hutch of the 1970s cop show Starsky and Hutch

e.etymology: The Hawaiian word for wind or breeze, used as a name for both boys and girls.
In the US mostly a K spelling of Cole, helped by Kol Mikaelson of The Vampire Diaries and The Originals. Kol is also an Albanian short form of Nikolle (Nicholas), and kol is Hebrew for voice.
A recent American coinage that adds the -ley ending of Kinsley and Finley to Quinn, an Irish surname from O Cuinn, descendant of Conn.
A respelling of Bellamy, an English surname from Norman French bel ami, fair friend. The -ie ending and the Bella nickname have made it a girls' name.
A respelling of Kailani, from Hawaiian kai, sea, and lani, sky or heaven, written with the Kay- of Kayla.
